Memory-controller charging, page-owner state, partition admission, memory acceptance and per-migration-type behavior.
Full layouts and invariants for page, folio, zone, zonelist, allocation context and processor-local cache objects.
Preemption, interrupt and locking rules for cache and zone locks aside from trial and nopin usage shown.
Default values, ranges and recomputation formulas for watermarks, reserves, ratios, batch sizes and statistical events.

findings.text: Bulk page acquisition fills a caller array up to a requested length, leaves already filled slots untouched, reports how many slots are filled on return, and diverts controller-accounted, single-remainder and page-owner-active requests to a single-page fallback path.

Bulk zone choice starts from a preferred entry, discards zones rejected by partitioning policy, refuses remote zones on multi-node machines, then tests each candidate against a low reserve increased by the still-missing count; candidates may be retried after on-demand acceptance or deferred growth, and absence of any qualifying zone triggers the single-page path.

When a qualifying zone is found the bulk path attempts a non-blocking grab of that zone processor-local cache, consumes only zero-order entries of the selected mobility class, initializes each taken descriptor for new use and marks it referenced, stops early if the cache empties after progress, and attributes allocation and zone statistics solely to newly taken entries.

A frozen allocator produces a descriptor that is not yet reference tracked while its sibling wrapper converts success into a tracked reference before returning; both accept request flags, size exponent, node preference, node mask and internal control bits.

Frozen acquisition validates control bits and size exponent, augments lockless requests with minimum-reserve and restricted flag subsets, normalizes flags through global allowance and current task context, builds a placement context, tries a fast freelist pass tuned against fragmentation and atomicity needs, retries through a slow reclaiming path when permitted, then either charges the controller or releases the result and reports failure, finally emitting tracing and sanitizer hooks.

Size exponents beyond the architectural maximum are rejected; lockless operation additionally requires that the exponent fit processor-local caching and is refused when non-blocking trial locking is unavailable or when deferred zone growth could require sleeping.

Convenience allocators resolve an unspecified node to the running node with an offline check, request compound grouping for folio creation, exclude high memory when returning directly addressable memory, and provide a zero-filled single-page variant.

Release helpers include grouped release of contiguous runs with scheduling courtesy, lockless single release, address-based release that ignores a null address yet validates genuine addresses, and sized release that walks page by page to the aligned end.

Exact-size acquisition derives an encompassing power-of-two order, discards compound and high-memory modifiers, obtains that order, then divides the result so leading pages covering the requested bytes stay allocated and referenced while trailing excess pages return to the order-zero tail pool.

Reserved deallocation checks alignment and maximum order, clears per-page tags, drops counts to zero, clears the reserved marker across the whole range, enlarges the managed total, and frees the range as frozen.

Processor-offline statistics handling moves per-processor event totals into the survivor, clears the departed differentials, merges zone and node deltas into shared counters with atomic addition, and propagates any global change into system-wide totals.

Processor lifecycle hooks drain reclaim, lock and cache state on departure and refresh processor-local cache thresholds on both departure and arrival; early initialization establishes per-zone caches, clears boot statistics for empty zones on NUMA builds, allocates per-node statistics for online nodes, and initializes deferred release machinery.

Bulk acquisition never blocks for the processor-local cache lock; a failed trial grab immediately diverts to the single-page path, and the lock is released before any fallback allocation or after the batch completes.

Cache-awareness updates guard a batch-retention flag with a non-pinning processor-local lock; writes to the pagelist fraction are serialized by a dedicated mutex while reads proceed without locking because torn reads are harmless.

Single-remainder bulk requests, controller-accounted bulk requests, page-owner-active bulk requests and zones lacking headroom all collapse to at most one page rather than failing outright; unmasked control bits, oversized orders and undersized fractions are treated as programming errors.

Tunable write handlers first delegate to a generic bounded integer or string parser and only on success refresh derived state: free-space minima and scaling factors rebuild watermarks, unmapped and slab ratios rebuild their minima, reserve ratios are staged through a temporary copy before commit, and fraction changes reprogram all populated zones.

A control table exposes tunable names for free-space minima, boost and scale factors, defragmentation mode, processor-local fraction, reserve ratios and, on NUMA builds, zonelist ordering plus unmapped and slab minima, each bound to its parser and current value with appropriate access and bounds.
Boot processor-local cache starts with high threshold 0 and batch size 1.
Zonelist order control stores at most 16 bytes and defaults to Node.
Lockless allocation implicitly requests warning suppression, zero filling, exclusion from emergency reserves and compound grouping.

Per-node load is held in an integer array indexed by node number up to the build-time node limit; boot caches and boot zone statistics exist as per-processor instances used before full setup and for unpopulated zones.
Zonelist order writes accept only initial letters D or N in either case and otherwise log a warning and reject with an invalid-argument error; reads delegate to generic string handling.

Processor cache awareness enables a high-batch retention flag when the per-processor data share shifted by page size exceeds three times the current batch, otherwise it clears the flag, applied across all populated zones.
